additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is defined by recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period with a sense of loss of control, accompanied by features such as rapid eating, eating until uncomfortably full, eating alone from embarrassment, and marked guilt or disgust afterward. It is distinguished from bulimia nervosa by the absence of regular compensatory behaviors, and it often becomes clinically apparent during periods of stress, transition, loneliness, or disrupted routines.

patient.stressor: Belinda’s closest bridge partner and longtime church friend died unexpectedly, leaving her to help organize the memorial luncheon, take over several community-center tasks, and face evenings that had once been filled with calls, quilting plans, and tournament gossip. During the following 5 months, she began keeping extra baked goods and potluck leftovers at home, then found herself eating unusually large amounts alone late at night, fast enough to feel painfully full and then deeply guilty. Because hospitality and self-control mattered so much in her Southern church circle, she became increasingly secretive and distressed about the contrast between her public competence and her private eating. She sought psychiatric care herself after a senior-center wellness talk on eating problems made her realize this was no longer ordinary grief eating.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On a bad night I can start with a plate of leftover funeral-luncheon casserole and before I know it I've eaten that, half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is in the fridge all in one sitting.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I take the first bite after the house is quiet, it's like my good sense steps aside, and even while I'm telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' my hands keep reaching for more.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast standing at the kitchen counter that I barely taste the pound cake or the crackers, and sometimes I catch myself swallowing before I've rightly chewed.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I keep going until my stomach is tight and sore under my nightgown and I have to ease myself into the recliner because moving around hurts.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: At bridge or church suppers I make a point of taking a modest little plate, then later after everyone has gone home I pull the leftovers out and eat in the kitchen where nobody can see me.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: I came because after these nights of eating I sit there with crumbs and empty containers around me feeling so ashamed and disgusted with myself that I can hardly pray or look folks at church in the eye the next morning.

add_requirements.The binge eating occurs, on average, at: Since my friend passed, these late-night eating spells have been happening at least once or twice most weeks, and there has not been a month where they really let up.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I have started turning down some bridge nights and church kitchen duties because I am so worried someone will notice the missing leftovers or ask why I seem ashamed.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months, ever since my closest bridge partner and church friend died.
